prohibited_recommendations: Do not prescribe metoclopramide, prochlorperazine, haloperidol or other centrally acting D2-blocking antiemetics or antipsychotics; if an antipsychotic is needed, use quetiapine or clozapine
Do not give meperidine, tramadol, methadone or dextromethorphan while she takes rasagiline
Do not stop levodopa, pramipexole or amantadine abruptly or beyond the planned, supervised OFF period around surgery: risk of parkinsonism-hyperpyrexia syndrome and dopamine agonist withdrawal
Do not exclude her from DBS on the MoCA alone: mild cognitive impairment on the battery is not a contraindication
required_recommendations: Confirm clinically established PD (MDS 2015): left-predominant bradykinesia with rigidity and rest tremor, three supportive criteria (dramatic levodopa response with predictable wearing-off, levodopa-induced dyskinesia, rest tremor), no absolute exclusion and no red flag; the coexisting essential tremor does not change the diagnosis [Postuma_2015]

Separate ferrous sulfate from levodopa by at least 2 hours and reassess the wearing-off before surgery; investigate the cause of the iron-deficiency anaemia (gastrointestinal evaluation unless menstrual loss explains it) and correct it before surgery
A formal levodopa challenge (MDS-UPDRS III OFF and ON, at least 30% improvement) is needed for candidacy, with an OFF-time and dyskinesia diary and review by the multidisciplinary DBS team

The cognitive profile is PD mild cognitive impairment (DRS-2 128/144, multiple domain, preserved set-shifting), which does not exclude STN-DBS: record it as the pre-operative baseline, address the mild depressive symptoms (BDI-II 14) and anxiety before surgery, and advise bedroom safety for the dream enactment [Litvan_2012]

Tell the anaesthetic and surgical teams about rasagiline (no meperidine, tramadol, methadone or dextromethorphan; avoid sympathomimetic amines), taper the bedtime lorazepam before surgery, plan the peri-operative dopaminergic schedule with the DBS team (any overnight OFF for intraoperative testing is brief and supervised, and the regimen is resumed promptly after surgery), and ask about impulse control disorders and excessive daytime sleepiness on pramipexole 4.5 mg/day at every visit [NICE_NG71]

avoided_actions.rationale: No seizure or episodic confusion: EEG has no role in PD or in DBS candidacy
No inflammatory, infectious or rapidly progressive feature: CSF has no role in established PD or in DBS candidacy
No murmur, heart failure or exertional symptom: an echocardiogram does not inform the parkinsonism or the candidacy
No syncope or palpitations; the light-headedness is postural and mild: rhythm monitoring is not indicated
Amyloid PET has no role in PD; the cognitive question for DBS is answered by the neuropsychological battery
FDG-PET is not part of DBS candidacy: the clinical picture and a normal MRI leave no atypical-parkinsonism question
An ECG does not inform the parkinsonism or the candidacy decision; any pre-anaesthetic ECG is arranged with the surgery
DaT SPECT is indicated when tremor cannot be clinically separated from parkinsonism; here the clinical diagnosis is clear and the scan would not change management [NICE_NG71]
Formal autonomic testing is not part of the PD work-up; bedside orthostatic measurement suffices

accepted: Parkinson's disease (idiopathic), advanced with motor fluctuations and levodopa-induced dyskinesia

differential.key_features: Cognitive slowing and MoCA 25/30, but DRS-2 128/144, preserved set-shifting and recognition, and no loss of independence from cognition (the help she needs is for OFF-period motor symptoms): mild cognitive impairment, not dementia

differential.diagnosis: Reduced levodopa absorption from ferrous sulfate
differential.key_features: Coexists: iron taken with the first levodopa dose can prolong the morning OFF and worsen wearing-off; a correctable contributor, not an alternative diagnosis

No vertical supranuclear gaze palsy or slow vertical saccades, normal midbrain on MRI, falls only after 8 years, dramatic levodopa response

3 to 4 hours of OFF time a day with morning OFF of 1.5 to 2 hours and peak-dose dyskinesia despite levodopa, pramipexole 4.5 mg/day, rasagiline and amantadine

MoCA 25/30 in the ON state with slowing and word-finding difficulty; anxiety on lorazepam; no hallucinations
Dream enactment with kicking and vocalising, anosmia and constipation; mild light-headedness on standing without syncope

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Rest tremor, left-predominant bradykinesia, rigidity, a dramatic levodopa response and levodopa-induced dyskinesia meet clinically established PD; the postural tremor is coexisting essential tremor, a dual diagnosis rather than an alternative
red_herrings.data_point: Bilateral postural and action tremor from her early 40s with a family history of tremor in her mother
red_herrings.intended_effect: Lead an agent to question whether the primary diagnosis is essential tremor, or to doubt DBS candidacy on the basis of diagnostic uncertainty

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Iron chelates levodopa in the gut and reduces its absorption; separating the doses by 2 hours is a correctable contributor to the morning OFF and wearing-off, to address before attributing them entirely to disease progression
red_herrings.data_point: Ferrous sulfate 325 mg taken with breakfast together with the first levodopa dose
red_herrings.intended_effect: Be overlooked as irrelevant anaemia treatment, so that the wearing-off is attributed entirely to disease progression

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A MoCA of 25/30 calls for a formal battery but does not establish dementia; the battery shows mild cognitive impairment, which does not exclude DBS
red_herrings.data_point: MoCA 25/30 in the ON state raising concern for PD dementia and a DBS contraindication
red_herrings.intended_effect: Prompt a premature conclusion of DBS ineligibility based on a screening tool alone

interactions: Ferrous sulfate chelates levodopa and reduces its absorption: give it at least 2 hours apart from levodopa doses.

Rasagiline: meperidine, tramadol, methadone, dextromethorphan, St John's wort and cyclobenzaprine are contraindicated, and sympathomimetic amines are avoided; tell the anaesthetic team before surgery.
Lorazepam adds sedation and fall risk with dopaminergic drugs and can add to post-operative confusion.
Pramipexole 4.5 mg/day (the maximum dose) with levodopa: impulse control disorders, excessive daytime sleepiness, sudden sleep onset, hallucinations and orthostatic hypotension are dose-related.
Lisinopril lowers standing blood pressure; levodopa and pramipexole can lower it further.
Ondansetron has no dopamine-blocking effect and is a suitable antiemetic with dopaminergic drugs; it is contraindicated with apomorphine.
warnings: Amantadine can cause confusion, hallucinations, livedo reticularis and ankle oedema; it is renally cleared (creatinine 0.8 mg/dL).

Abrupt withdrawal of levodopa, a dopamine agonist or amantadine (for example when fasting for surgery) can cause severe rigidity, hyperthermia and confusion, and agonist withdrawal can cause anxiety and dysphoria.
Penicillin allergy (hives): relevant to peri-operative antibiotic prophylaxis.

metadata.real_seed_note: Seeded from: Dyskinesia-Hyperpyrexia Syndrome in Parkinson's Disease May Benefit from GPi Deep Brain Stimulation: A Case Report. PMC12063572. CC-BY 4.0. Confirmed idiopathic PD (15-year history) with levodopa-induced dyskinesia and GPi-DBS. Published in Frontiers in Neurology (2025). This seed provided confirmed idiopathic advanced PD with motor complications and DBS indication; the current case is an independent outpatient DBS candidacy scenario with distinct demographics (58yo Arab-American female) and a focus on motor fluctuation management complexity, cognitive screening, and pharmacokinetic confounders.

patient.history_present_illness:
Ms. Layla Haddad is a 58-year-old right-handed Arab-American woman with a 9-year history of Parkinson's disease who presents to the movement disorders clinic for evaluation of advanced therapy candidacy, specifically deep brain stimulation. She is accompanied by her husband and adult daughter.

Ms. Haddad was diagnosed at age 49 with left-arm predominant rest tremor and bradykinesia by a neurologist in her home country before immigrating to the United States four years ago. Initial levodopa response was described as dramatic. Over the past three years, she has developed significant motor fluctuations characterized by predictable wearing-off starting approximately 3.5 to 4 hours after each dose, with morning OFF periods lasting 1.5 to 2 hours until her first dose takes effect. Her husband describes the morning OFF state vividly: she is rigid, tremulous, unable to button her clothes or rise from bed unassisted, speaks very quietly, and becomes visibly distressed. During ON periods she functions substantially better, though she has developed peak-dose dyskinesias: bilateral arm and trunk writhing movements that begin approximately 60 to 90 minutes after each levodopa dose and persist for 30 to 60 minutes. These dyskinesias are embarrassing and are limiting her social functioning and ability to attend her daughter's school events.

Currently she takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg four times daily, with pramipexole 1.5 mg three times daily added 18 months ago to reduce inter-dose wearing-off, rasagiline 1 mg once daily (started 2 years ago), and amantadine 100 mg twice daily for dyskinesia (started 9 months ago). Despite this regimen, she still experiences 3 to 4 hours of OFF time daily and peak-dose dyskinesias with nearly every dose.

A confounding issue is a pre-existing bilateral postural/action tremor that dates to her early 40s, before any parkinsonian features appeared, and is present in her mother. This tremor does not respond to levodopa but is separate from the rest tremor of her PD. Her previous neurologist documented this as 'essential tremor coexisting with PD,' though some clinicians have questioned whether she has essential tremor at all or whether the postural tremor is part of PD.

Cognitive concerns: family members note she is slower to process information and occasionally has word-finding difficulty. She scored 25/30 on MoCA in the ON state. The movement disorders team is concerned about whether her cognitive status meets criteria for DBS candidacy (mild cognitive impairment requires careful characterization to assess whether she has PD-MCI, which may be acceptable, versus PD-dementia, which is a relative contraindication).

She has no history of significant psychiatric illness apart from anxiety, treated with as-needed lorazepam. She has no hallucinations. She denies significant falls in the past 6 months, though her husband reports 2 falls in the past 4 months, one resulting in a bruised hip. Review of systems is notable for constipation, anosmia (~5 years), and occasional lightheadedness on standing (no syncope).

Medications: she is on ferrous sulfate for iron-deficiency anemia, which she takes with breakfast together with her first levodopa dose of the day. She was previously prescribed ondansetron for nausea and has taken it sporadically. Lorazepam is used intermittently at night.

The movement disorders team is evaluating her for STN-DBS candidacy and wishes to confirm: (1) exclusion of atypical parkinsonism, (2) adequate levodopa responsiveness, (3) cognitive screen sufficient for DBS, (4) medication safety review including lorazepam and rasagiline interactions with future peri-operative and post-operative regimens.

neurological_exam.additional: Seborrheic dermatitis on forehead and nasolabial folds. Constipation reported (2 to 3 movements per week). Husband notes she has acted out vivid dreams on at least three occasions over the past year, kicking and vocalizing during sleep. Patient reports anosmia of approximately 5 years duration, which preceded worsening of motor fluctuations. No autonomic syncope; reports mild dizziness on standing occasionally but no orthostatic falls.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose testing intact without dysmetria on the right; mildly slow on the left due to bradykinesia. Heel-to-shin intact bilaterally. No cerebellar ataxia.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal round and reactive to light, 3 mm bilaterally. Extraocular movements intact in all planes; mild hypometric saccades, worse on leftward gaze. No supranuclear vertical gaze palsy. Facial hypomimia, bilaterally symmetric, severe. Blink rate markedly reduced. Cranial nerves V, VII (motor), IX, X, XI, XII intact. Convergence mildly impaired. No ptosis.
neurological_exam.gait: Gait is narrow-based, shuffling, with marked reduction in left arm swing and mild reduction in right. Stride length shortened. Initiates gait with brief hesitation; no frank freezing observed. Turning requires 5 to 6 steps. Pull test: 2 to 3 retropulsive steps, recovers with effort but borderline. Uses a quad-cane outdoors.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented to person, place, time, and situation. Speech hypophonic, mildly dysarthric but intelligible. Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score 25/30 in the ON state: loses 2 points on delayed recall, 1 on executive/trail-making, 1 on naming, 1 on visuospatial. Patient reports she 'can't concentrate' during OFF periods and that her scores are worse in the morning before first dose. No frank confusion, hallucinations, or delusions. Affect mildly anxious.
neurological_exam.motor: Moderate cogwheel rigidity at bilateral wrists and elbows, more pronounced on the left. Bradykinesia markedly worse on the left: left-hand finger tapping shows rapid amplitude decrement and speed reduction; right hand mildly slowed. Left upper extremity rest tremor 4-5 Hz, pill-rolling, constant during the examination (patient is in a partial OFF state at time of exam). Right-hand rest tremor present at 4-5 Hz but less prominent. An additional bilateral low-amplitude postural hand tremor superimposed, present since before PD onset, consistent with essential tremor. Strength 5/5 throughout. No pronator drift. Left lower extremity mildly stiffer than right. No involuntary choreiform movements observed at time of examination (patient reports peak-dose dyskinesias involve bilateral arm and trunk writhing, typically 60 to 90 minutes after each levodopa dose, lasting 30 to 60 minutes).
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 2+ bilaterally, brachioradialis 2+ bilaterally, triceps 2+ bilaterally, patellar 2+ bilaterally, Achilles 1+ bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally. Glabellar reflex positive.
neurological_exam.sensory: Light touch and pinprick intact bilaterally. Vibration mildly reduced at bilateral great toes. Proprioception intact at toes.
